titre: The Night Watch: A Nickname Attested in 1797, a Painting Trimmed
accroche: The painting originally had no title, does not depict a night scene, and lost four pieces in 1715.
contenu_vulgarise:
*The Night Watch* gives the impression of a night scene: armed men emerging from a dark background. Yet the name, the size, and the darkness of the painting we look at today each have a history separate from that of its painting.

The painting is signed and dated “Rembrandt f 1642.” Rembrandt received the commission before December 1640, for a company of the civic guard of District II of Amsterdam, under the command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq. The Rijksmuseum, which holds it, specifies that originally the work had no title. The nickname “Night Watch,” which the French render as *La Ronde de nuit*, appears for the first time in a document from 1797, 155 years after the painting. The title the Rijksmuseum gives it today describes a militia company, not a patrol.

## A Name Born of Varnish?

This nickname is often attributed to the painting's appearance. For a long time, it is said, it was covered with a blackened varnish, which gave the whole the look of a night scene. This dark varnish was removed only in the 1940s. The Rijksmuseum dates to 1947 the varnish then applied to the painting, a mastic that had become brittle and yellowed. The nickname, for its part, was already established, and it stuck. What is established is the 1797 date and the absence of an original title; the causal link between the varnish and the nickname is a common explanation, not a certainty.

## A Painting Cut Down

The trimming is the best-documented part. In 1715, the painting leaves the Kloveniersdoelen for Amsterdam's town hall, on Dam Square, today the Royal Palace. A resolution from that year orders it cleaned and placed in the Small War Council chamber. To make it fit between two doors, four pieces are cut off, according to the Rijksmuseum, the largest on the left. None of these pieces has ever been found.

## What Is Missing

According to Wikipedia, two figures on the left, the top of the archway, the balustrade, and the edge of the step were on the pieces removed. The painting suffered other attacks, much later: on September 14, 1975, a knife attack leaves 12 slashes; in 1990, an acid attack damages only the varnish, thanks to a guard's quick reaction, according to the Rijksmuseum.

quiz.question: Why is The Night Watch smaller today than when Rembrandt finished it?
choix: Rembrandt himself reduced it in 1642, after the protest of the militiamen who had commissioned it
It was cut down in 1715 to fit between two doors of the town hall
The knife slashes of 1975 forced the restorers to remove the damaged areas of the canvas
quiz.explication: The painting is completed in 1642 and moved in 1715, 73 years later, to a location where it has to be made to fit between two doors: four pieces are cut off, the largest on the left. Rembrandt did not reduce it, and the cuts predate the 1975 knife attack by more than two centuries.

choix: In 1642, the very year the painting was completed
In 1715, when it was moved to the town hall
In 1947, when the varnish was removed
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Rijksmuseum specifies that the nickname first appears in a document from 1797, 155 years after Rembrandt completed the canvas in 1642.
